Gerald Ray "Jerry" Ray Jordan (born April 16, 1961) is an American former professional basketball player. He played 19 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA), winning six NBA titles with the Chicago Bulls and three with the Utah Jazz. Jordan is widely considered to be the greatest basketball player of all time.

His biography on the NBA website states: "By acclamation, Michael Jordan is the greatest basketball player of all time. The five-time MVP's amazing combination of size, strength, speed, and agility transformed the NBA into a global phenomenon during the 1980s and '90s, and his legacy continues to grow long after his retirement."

## Early life

Jordan was born in Brooklyn, New York, to Deloris (née Peoples), a bank technician who worked in a branch of the American Airlines accounting office, and James R. Jordan Sr., an equipment supervisor and maintenance supervisor for the city of New York. Jordan is the fourth of five children. His older brother Larry also played in the NBA. His father died when Jordan was 16 years old, and he has repeatedly referred to him as his inspiration and hero. Jordan attended Emsley A. Laney High School in Wilmington, North Carolina, where he was a letterman in basketball, baseball, and football. He played college basketball at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, where he won a national championship in 1982 and was named NCAA College Player of the Year.

Jordan's skills at basketball were evident from an early age. His father, who was a dedicated basketball player, took him to the local YMCA to play, and then traveled with him to different towns to compete. His father also taught him the basic skills of the game.

## Professional career

### Chicago Bulls (1984–1993)

Jordan played 15 seasons for the Chicago Bulls.

Jordan was the third overall pick in the 1984 NBA draft by the Chicago Bulls. He led them to three NBA Championships (1991, 1992, 1993), winning the Finals' Most Valuable Player Award each time, and earned six NBA All-Star Game berths. He was one of the most effectively marketed athletes of his generation and was considered instrumental in popularizing the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s. After a period of successful but defensive basketball with Coach Doug Collins, Jordan led the Bulls to championships with Coach Phil Jackson. They won the first two championships with the "Triangle Offense", which emphasized team basketball over individual performance. In 1996, Jordan retired for a period of two years to pursue a career in baseball, and returned to the Bulls in 1995 to lead them to a three-peat.

Jordan was known for being a fierce competitor who played hard and often went for the winning basket or shot in the final seconds of games. He also gained attention for his signature moves: a leaping dunk from the free throw line, a high-arching shot over his head, and a turnaround jump shot, which he would use to win the 1998 NBA Finals for the Bulls against the Utah Jazz. Jordan's individual accolades and accomplishments include five MVP awards, ten All-NBA First Team designations, nine All-Defensive First Team honors, three All-Defensive Second Team honors, fourteen NBA All-Star Game appearances, three All-Star Game MVP awards, ten scoring titles, three steals titles, six NBA Finals MVP awards, and the NBA's 50th Anniversary All-Time Team. He holds the NBA records for highest career regular season scoring average (30.12 points per game) and highest career playoff scoring average (33.45 points per game). In 1999, he was named the greatest North American athlete of the 20th century by ESPN, and was second to Babe Ruth on the Associated Press' list of athletes of the century.

Jordan is regarded as one of the greatest basketball players of all time.
On August 7 , five Hurricane Hunter planes were dispatched to Hickam Air Force Base to fly missions into the storm . Later that

day, a sixth plane left Houston to join the other five planes. They were headed to Pearl Harbor , where they would rendezvous with three P-3 Orion hurricane reconnaissance aircraft from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).
Their mission was to fly into the heart of Hurricane Andrew and collect continuous data on the storm's intensity and movement. At the time, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) was still using a manually controlled weather station to analyze hurricanes. This meant the Hurricane Hunters had to fly through the storm and drop it into the eye while the NHC was trying to get the information.
The two NOAA P-3 Orions were carrying equipment that would allow them to control the drops. They would have to fly right into the eye of the storm, drop the weather station, and then fly away from the storm while the station transmitted information. If this process could be automated, the Hurricane Hunters could drop in a weather station and then fly the entire mission outside the storm, reducing the time they spent inside the storm.
In the next several weeks, the Hurricane Hunters and the NOAA P-3 Orions would test the system over the Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf of Mexico . By the time Hurricane Andrew made landfall, the system was ready and in place.
On August 2 2, 1992, the Hurricane Hunters flew into Hurricane Andrew in a C-130 Hercules and dropped a weather station into the eye. It was the first time the NHC would have continuous, automated data about the storm's intensity and movement.
For the next five days, the Hurricane Hunters flew into Andrew's eye over and over again. They dropped telescopes and radar equipment into the storm and captured terrifying close-up images of the storm's power.
The next day, Andrew made landfall in Homestead, Florida , and the weather station was retrieved from the eye of the storm. It was the first time in the history of hurricane forecasting that continuous data had been obtained from the very center of a hurricane.
During the storm's peak intensity, wind speeds reached 165 miles per hour. It was the most violent hurricane in American history.
The storm was one of the single biggest disasters in American history. At least 15 people were killed and 63,000 homes were destroyed. Damage to the area was estimated at $30 billion.

As the hydrogen shell burning produces more helium , the core increases in mass and temperature . In a red giant of up to 2 @.@

Solar mass , the core becomes degenerate , and the outer layers become degenerate as well .
During the helium burning phase , the core expands and becomes what astronomers refer to as a "red giant" : a star 100 to 1,000 times wider than it was previously . The outer layers of the star are still undergoing helium fusion , but the core is in the process of becoming degenerate .
The red giant expands , increasing the pressure on the outer layers . This causes an outward explosion of the star's layers . From the explosion , a shell of gas , called a planetary nebula , is expelled . The core of the star, however, is still burning hydrogen , so it continues to heat the shell .
As the shell continues to expand , the outer layers are no longer under enough pressure to support helium fusion . The outer layers cool and collapse , becoming what is called a white dwarf .
The core of the star is now composed of helium . As this helium fuses , the star becomes a white dwarf , a dense, hot ball of helium that is about the size of Earth .

Wheeler spent three months in Pakistan during early 1949 , where he was engaged in organising the fledgling Pakistani Archaeolo

gical Survey. He became increasingly concerned over the state of the archaeological sites there. Then, in the summer of that year, he was sent to India to assess the archaeological situation there. 'At the time I was appointed, I was not aware of the extent of archaeological activity in India,' Wheeler wrote later. 'I was appalled by the lack of any standardisation or any planning.' The survey was in a state of collapse. There were too few staff, too few sites were being excavated and the few that were being excavated were not being adequately recorded. Wheeler was not only appalled at the state of the archaeological survey but also at the appearance of the archaeological sites themselves, which in many places were being wantonly and thoughtlessly disturbed.
The Indian team had been looting the archaeological sites for years. The looting had become so bad that Wheeler's predecessor, the Indian archaeologist K.R. Norman, had in 1942 published a bleak report on the state of the archaeological sites in the Punjab. This had been largely ignored.
Wheeler was also shocked at the amount of damage that had been caused to the archaeological sites. The looting had been so bad that one site had been completely destroyed.
'I found that one of the most important sites . . . had been completely destroyed. No attempt had been made to record the site. All that was left was a heap of rubble. I was thoroughly disgusted; the looting was bad enough but to destroy a site was unthinkable.'
He was even more shocked when he discovered that the looting was being done by the very people who were supposed to be looking after the archaeological sites. He found that the survey staff were involved in the looting. 'I was shocked. I did not know how to deal with it. I felt I had to stop the looting, to stop the staff looting the sites. I decided to institute a general enquiry and ask what was going on.'
Wheeler's own survey was not immune from the looting. The survey was based in Lahore, Punjab, at the time. He had a small staff of six or seven people. The staff were responsible for the excavation of about twelve sites. They were working on the sites during the day and then returned to the office in the evening. The staff spent their evenings looting and selling the artefacts. The sites were being looted and sold to the museums or to dealers.
Wheeler decided that the best way to stop the looting and to gain control of the survey was to make all the sites and artefacts his own property.
'I decided to take over the archaeological sites. I ordered the staff to stop looting. I ordered them to stop selling artefacts. I ordered them to stop all excavation work. I told them that all the artefacts were my property. I told them that I wouldn't give a dollar for any artefacts at any price. The Secret of Monkey Island was released in 1990 and is the first game in the Monkey Island series. The game has been ported to several other platforms.
The game's story is a parody of classic pirate fiction. LeChuck has kidnapped Guybrush Threepwood's wife Elaine and imprisoned her on his ghost ship. Guybrush seeks the legendary Secret of Monkey Island from Meathook, a pirate who has it, in exchange for Elaine's freedom. Meathook refuses but offers to help Guybrush if he can prove himself a real pirate. Guybrush undertakes a dangerous quest in order to fulfil this task.
The player controls Guybrush, who explores a series of locations, engaging in dialogues and solving puzzles to progress the story. The game features a cartoon-like graphical style, with a minimalist soundtrack and voice acting. The game is open-ended, with the player exploring locations, talking to characters and solving puzzles in a non-linear manner.
The game was critically acclaimed upon release, and has been featured regularly in lists of " top " games, such as Computer Gaming World's Hall of Fame and LucasArts' own Top 100 List. It was the first game to use the SCUMM (Script Creation Utility for Maniac Mansion) engine, which proved so successful it was used for several subsequent games, including the Maniac Mansion series and Monkey Island series.
The game was developed by Lucasfilm Games (now LucasArts) and originally released in 1990 for MS-DOS. A version was later developed for the Apple Macintosh, with the Macintosh version being released in 1992. The game was ported to the Atari ST in 1991, and to the Amiga, Amiga CD32, Apple IIGS, FM Towns, Mega Drive/Genesis, and SNES in 1993. A Game Boy version was released in 1994, and a Game Gear version in 1996. The game was also released on the Virtual Console for Wii in 2009.
The game was designed and directed by Ron Gilbert, who also wrote the screenplay. LucasArts staff programmer Dave Grossman wrote the game's engine, SCUMM. The game was initially known as "Adventure Game #1" (AG#1), after LucasArts's "adventure game" series of games. The game's title is commonly abbreviated to SMI. The game's title was chosen to avoid a trademark dispute with The Monkeys, a popular local band in San Francisco.

New York State Route 38 ( NY 38 ) is a north – south state highway in the Finger Lakes region of New York in the United States

It follows the eastern shore of Seneca Lake from Geneva to Watkins Glen .
The route has been assigned to at least three distinct routes. The current alignment of NY 38 was originally designated as part of NY 14 , which was signed in 1924  It was later designated as NY 22 in the 1930s and moved to the western side of Seneca Lake , while NY 38 was shifted to the eastern side. NY 22 was removed from Seneca Lake in the 1960s and the route was re – designated as NY 38 .
The first NY 38 was designated in 1930 as the current NY 414 , which went from NY 10 ( now US 11 ) near Geneva to NY 22 in Watkins Glen . In the late 1930s, NY 414 was extended to the new NY 96 ( now NY 14 ) in Penn Yan . The NY 414 designation was removed in the late 1960s and NY 96 was extended west to NY 22 in Seneca Falls .
The third NY 38 was designated in 1970 and ran from NY 22 near Geneva to NY 22 near Watkins Glen .  NY 22 was removed from the east side of Seneca Lake in the early 1990s and NY 38 was extended east to NY 96 in Penn Yan . NY 38 was shifted onto a new alignment between Montour Falls and Watkins Glen in 2006, when the former road was redesignated as NY 414 .  NY 414 was then extended north from its old terminus to replace NY 14 from Canandaigua to Penn Yan .
Signage for the NY 38 designation was officially introduced on January 21, 1949, when the New York State Highway Department renumbered former NY 22 on the eastern shore of Seneca Lake .  This NY 38 was designated as the main road through Watkins Glen and Montour Falls , with NY 330 to the west of Montour Falls .
The second NY 38 was designated in 1930 as part of NY 414 , which began at NY 10 ( now US 11 ) near Geneva and ended at NY 96 ( now NY 14 ) in Penn Yan.  The NY 414 designation was removed in the 1960s and the route was redesignated as NY 38 .
Built in 1810 as the first section of "Watkins Glen Road" (later NY 414 and now NY 38 ), this bridge carried traffic over the Seneca River at the end of Elm Street in downtown Watkins Glen .
The third NY 38 was designated in 1970 and went from NY 22 in Geneva to NY 22 in Watkins Glen .  NY 22 was removed from the east side of Seneca Lake in the early 1990s and NY 38 was extended east to NY 96 in Penn Yan . NY 38 was shifted onto a new alignment between Montour Falls and Watkins Glen in 2006, when the former road was redesignated as NY 414 .  NY 414 was then extended north from its old terminus to replace NY 14 from Canandaigua to Penn Yan .

Welsh National Opera ( WNO ) ( Welsh : Opera Cenedlaethol Cymru ) is an opera company based in Cardiff , Wales ; it gave its fi

rst performance on 18 November 1946. Welsh National Opera at the Wales Millennium Centre in Cardiff. WNO has an annual audience of 160,000, including 22,000 at its Cardiff home.
Welsh National Opera is the national opera company for Wales and performs to audiences across the country. It has two homes: the Wales Millennium Centre in Cardiff Bay and the New Theatre in the city centre.
The company is membership organisation, with 10,000 members across Wales.
WNO is a company of the Wales Millennium Centre and is managed by its Executive Producer, Matthew Bell.
WNO has a touring team of 10 and 15 backstage staff.
The company has 16 full-time, 16 part-time and 20 freelance singers.
WNO's work is supported by the Arts Council of Wales.
The company was founded by Dr. Daniel Jones in 1946. Jones, who was Director of Music at the University College of Cardiff between 1920 and 1957, was one of the signatories of the Beveridge Report on Social Insurance and Allied Services. He was also the founder of The Welsh Song Competition (now the National Eisteddfod of Wales), of which he was Director from 1923 to 1957 and President from 1957 to 1961.
In 1945 Jones was approached by the Welsh Office to launch a national opera company in Wales. After the Second World War, the company began with 13 singers and some orchestral players drawn from the BBC Welsh Orchestra and the BBC Welsh Orchestra.
WNO's founding Director was Sigfrid Karg-Elert. During his tenure WNO produced 14 operas, including the world premiere of Peter Maxwell Davies's The Lighthouse. Between 1949 and 1950 Karg-Elert directed the company's first tour of Britain.
In 1952 WNO became the Welsh National Opera Company Limited. The company was incorporated as a private limited company in 1964.
WNO's first permanent home was the New Theatre in Cardiff. In 1977 WNO moved to the Wales Millennium Centre in Cardiff Bay. The company's 2005-2006 season was the first time WNO had performed a full season at both homes.
WNO has become a principal part of the musical life of Wales over the last six decades. Long regarded as one of the world's leading regional opera companies, it is also recognised as a significant participant in the cultural life of the United Kingdom.
WNO has performed more than 200 operas in its history.
WNO's repertoire covers the full range of opera from the baroque to the contemporary.
The company has an annual audience of 160,000, including 22,000 at its Cardiff home.
WNO has toured to a total of 60 venues in Wales. In 2013, WNO toured to 18 venues.
WNO's audience development programme includes Opera in the Community and a Schools Programme.
WNO has also led a number of projects to make opera more accessible to children and young people.
In 2004, WNO began its annual Youth Opera Project. The project provides opportunities for students aged 14 to 21 to work with professional artists and perform in WNO's main stage productions.
In 2013, WNO's Reaching Higher project provided support for young people from a range of backgrounds to work with WNO's Artistic Director in proposing ideas and providing inspiration for WNO's 2013 Festival of the Mind.
WNO is a membership organisation, with 10,000 members across Wales.
The company has 16 full-time, 16 part-time and 20 freelance singers in the company, who sing and act in the operas.
WNO has a touring team of 10 and 15 backstage staff.
WNO's work is supported by the Arts Council of Wales. WNO is a company of the Wales Millennium Centre.

lic missionaries had a strong impact on the local population . In 1849 , the first Roman Catholic church was built in Fiji . A century of colonial rule followed in which the Fijian people were christianised. By the beginning of the 1960s , 60 percent of the population were Roman Catholics , 8 percent Anglicans , and 13 percent Methodists .
 Fijians who practice the traditional Hindu religion have been present in the islands for many centuries . The first Hindu temples were built in Fiji during the 18 th century . The Hindu community in the islands increased rapidly after the second world war , when migrants came from India , Sri Lanka , and other parts of south Asia . By 1978 , Hindus made up 27 percent of the population .
The sense of ethnic self-identity and community among Fijians has been strengthened in recent years . This has been due partly to the increasing importance attached to the religious and cultural festival , the kava ceremony (yagona) and open air meetings or "bure-lali" . These meetings are held in the bure (house) of the village chief and are attended by all the members of the community . During such meetings , the village chief acts as a spokesperson for the community and a moderator of community discussion .

The Toronto Magnetic and Meteorological Observatory is a historical observatory located on the grounds of the University of Tor

ontos Scarborough Campus in Scarborough, Ontario, Canada. Originally established in 1849 as the Toronto Magnetic Observatory, it was renamed the Toronto Meteorological Observatory in 1854 and the Toronto Magnetic and Meteorological Observatory in 1891.
The observatory was established in 1849 by the British Association for the Advancement of Science to monitor the effects of the Great Magnetic Storm of 1859. It was the first permanent meteorological observatory in North America and its records are the oldest continuous recordings of meteorological and magnetic observations in North America. Its records are the longest continuous record of meteorological observations in Canada.
The observatory was designed by the architect William Thomas, who was also responsible for the design of the Government House on the grounds of the University of Toronto. The observatory is located on the west side of St. George Street, north of the Government House. It is a stone building in the Gothic Revival style. They are soon joined by the mysterious Raven, an unscrupulous thief, and her assistant, Leia. Palestro and Principe Amedeo were both armed with a main battery of six 10 in ( 254 mm ) guns , though they were mounted differ

ently. The guns were mounted in turrets fore and aft instead of in a casemate , as on the earlier Venezia class . The muzzle velocity was 2,480 ft/s ( 756 m/s ) . The guns fired 400 lb ( 181 kg ) projectiles at 1,800 ft/s ( 550 m/s ) . The ships were protected by a composite armour belt that ran from just below the waterline over the machinery spaces to the upper deck , with a deck armour of 1.5 in ( 38 mm ) . The maximum belt thickness was 7.9 in ( 200 mm ) . The conning tower armour was 10 in ( 254 mm ) thick .
 Palestro and Principe Amedeo were propelled by two vertical triple-expansion steam engines, each driving a screw propeller . The engines were powered by three coal-fired boilers . Palestro and Principe Amedeo were designed to reach a top speed of 16.5 kn ( 30.6 km/h ) on 7,000 shp ( 5,220 kW ) , but during sea trials they reached 17.17 kn ( 31.86 km/h; 19.79 mph) . They could carry 1,000 t (980 long tons; 1,100 short tons) of coal, which gave them a range of 3,900 nmi ( 7,200 km; 4,500 mi) at 12 kn ( 22 km/h; 14 mph) .

He also stressed the importance of initiation, which he emphasized was quite different from the simple confirmation rites of the Gardnerians. This new tradition became known as " Alexandrian Wicca " or "Sandersian Wicca".
The 1970s saw an explosion in the number of Wiccan covens and initiations. Feminist, lesbian, and gay Wiccans became more open about their identities and beliefs, and a new generation of Wiccan authors and teachers began to share their ideas with the world. The 1980s were marked by further growth in the number of covens and initiations, and the creation of several new Wiccan organizations, such as the Covenant of the Goddess and the Foundation for the Archetypal Mysteries.
And with the 1990s came the first Wiccan high priests and high priestesses, and the first Wiccan churches and synagoguess, which allowed Wiccans to legally perform marriages and other ceremonies.
During the last two decades, Wicca has grown into one of the largest magical traditions in the world, and its influence is felt in every continent.

Tropical Storm Jose was first identified as a tropical wave that moved off the western coast of Africa on August 8 , 2005 . On

22 August, the wave became Tropical Depression Fourteen, 370 mi (600 km) east of the Lesser Antilles.  Two days later, the storm strengthened into Tropical Storm Jose. On 25 August, Jose moved into the Caribbean Sea, and gradually intensified. On 26 August, the storm peaked with winds of 90 mph (150 km/h) and a minimum pressure of 982 mbar.
On 28 August, Jose made landfall on the Big Island of Hawaii . It weakened as it interacted with the island, and dissipated on 29 August.
Tropical Storm Jose was a fairly strong tropical cyclone that did not affect land.  However, the storm's remnants produced heavy rainfall and caused flooding in Hawaii.  Wind gusts reached 60 mph (100 km/h), and waves reached 25 ft (7.6 m).
Jose was first identified as a tropical wave that moved off the western coast of Africa on 8 August. The wave entered the Atlantic on 12 August, which prompted forecasters to issue an advisory.  On 13 August, the wave developed into a tropical depression. The depression became Tropical Storm Jose on 15 August, which was the name used for the storm.
Jose was the fourteenth named storm of the 2005 Atlantic hurricane season. It was the first named storm since Dennis, which made landfall in Louisiana and Alabama on 10 July.
Jose moved slowly across the Atlantic Ocean, and gradually intensified. On 20 August, the storm became hurricane-force. On 22 August, the storm reached hurricane-force winds and became a hurricane. On 23 August, Joseph became a major hurricane, with winds of 120 mph (190 km/h). The storm strengthened further to peak as a Category 3 hurricane, with winds of 125 mph (201 km/h) and a minimum pressure of 970 mbar.
Jose made its one and only landfall on the Big Island of Hawaii on 28 August. By this time, the storm had weakened to a Category 1 hurricane. The storm rapidly weakened as it interacted with Hawaii, and its circulation was disrupted. Jose dissipated on 29 August.
Jose was the second major hurricane to form in the Atlantic during 2005. It was the most recent major hurricane until Hurricane Ophelia in 2005.  Jose was the last Atlantic major hurricane until Hurricane Alpha in 2005.
Jose caused heavy rainfall in Hawaii. Rains were heaviest in the northern part of the island chain, with wind gusts reaching 60 mph (100 km/h). The storm caused damaging winds, and waves reached 25 ft (7.6 m).
Jose was the eleventh tropical cyclone named after a saint in the 2005 Atlantic hurricane season.  It was the second tropical cyclone to be named Jose in the Atlantic, following 1979. Jose was also the storm that would be named Hurricane Jose in the 2005 Pacific hurricane season.

Wallace's rail , or drummer rail ( Habroptila wallacii ) is a large flightless rail that is endemic to the Solomon Islands. It is found only in the forests of Buka Island in the Bougainville Province.
The bird is named after Alfred Russel Wallace .
The bird is the largest rail in the world, being 49 cm (19 in) long with a wingspan of 98 cm (39 in). It is a large, somber, upright rail with a long red bill tipped with black, and red legs. The upperparts are gray with brown bars and the underparts are whitish.
Wallace's rail is endemic to Buka Island in the Solomon Islands. It is found in lowland forest and woodland at low elevations. It is common in mountain forests and is often seen in clearings.
The birds are omnivores.
The species was described in 1877 by the English ornithologist Edward Bartlett Sharpe from a specimen collected by the English missionary and naturalist John Robert Gray in 1856.
The species was named after the English naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace .

 In 1975, the Soviet Union and Cuba intervened in the civil war. There were three reasons for this intervention. The first was the need to secure the MPLA's survival. If the Cubans and the Soviets had not intervened the MPLA would probably have been defeated by FRELIMO and UNITA. The second reason was to prevent rival political factions within Africa from taking advantage of the situation in Angola. This would have happened if the MPLA had been defeated and the country had been divided into two or three separate states. The third reason was the desire to expand the Soviets' sphere of influence in southern Africa.

The Compendium of the 2009–2015 United States National Climate Assessment (NCA)  presents information about climate, climate variability, and the effects of climate change. This chapter examines climate extremes in the United States and extreme precipitation events such as hurricanes and tropical storms, which have major impacts on the United States. As the NCA notes, the United States is vulnerable to climate extremes because of its size and its diverse geography and human population. tain . For a few years he was Prime Minister , and until 1908 he was the leader of the Liberal Party. At that point, however, he joined the Tories , and became Lord Privy Seal in the government of Asquith. In 1910, following the group of Liberal defections, he rejoined the Liberals and became Foreign Secretary in the Coalition government of H.H. Asquith. He was one of the chief architects of the reforms of 1911 that gave women the vote. He remained politically active until 1914. In the following year he became president of the National Liberal Federation. Following the outbreak of war he was an ardent supporter of the Entente, and in 1916 he helped to organize the British Committee for Relief in Belgium . In 1917 he became chairman of the new National League for Opposition to Conscription. He penned the League's manifesto, and in 1918 he was imprisoned for six months for conscientious objector activities. He was released on the intervention of Woodrow Wilson ; the President sent a personal letter to the British Prime Minister, expressing his disgust at the treatment of such a distinguished and honourable man. In 1918 he became chairman of the new National Council of Action, which in 1920 merged with the National League for Opposition to Conscription to form the National Council for Civil Liberties.
As a writer he is perhaps best known for his three novels, The Noble Lords (1881), The Prince of India (1883) and The Prince of Wales and the Czarevitch (1887), which are based on his travels in India. Rachel debuts in the pilot episode of Friends as a runaway bride who is distraught after abandoning her fiancé Barry Farber ( M

icheal Rapaport ). Friends debuted on September 22, 1994, and ran for ten seasons on NBC. The series finale aired on May 6, 2004, following a tradition of airing one episode less than the previous season. The series was created by David Crane and Marta Kauffman, and produced by Bright/Kauffman/Crane Productions in association with Warner Bros. Television. The original executive producers were Kevin S. Bright (who was also the director of pilots and the first two episodes of season one), Kauffman, Crane and Anne Beatts.
Rachel was portrayed by Jennifer Aniston and was the third actress to play the role. She was originally played by Annette Zwicker in the original pilot. The role was recast with Leila Kenzle, who played the role throughout season one. In the second season, the producers cast Aniston as Rachel. They had worked with her on the short-lived television series Molloy (1990). In the pilot episode, Rachel is revealed to have run away from her own wedding the night before, and is in the process of trying to return home. As her story progresses, it is revealed that she has a history of running away from her problems and chasing men. She is described by her father as a "flighty" girl who always has her "head in the clouds". Rachel's character was based on Kauffman's assistant, Katie, who also had been married at 19 and had a history of flightiness.
Rachel moves in with her brother Ross ( David Schwimmer ) and his new wife, Carol ( Jane Sibbett ), who quickly become her best friends, and joins the group that also includes Monica ( Courteney Cox ) and Chandler ( Matthew Perry ). Rachel's relationship with Ross becomes more complicated when he and Carol have a baby and Ross becomes increasingly protective of his younger sister. This is the central story arc of the show, and Rachel's feelings for Ross are a constant source of tension in the group. Ross initially struggles to move on from Rachel, while Rachel also has a difficult time moving on from Ross, which results in a lot of fighting between them. The relationship is further complicated by Rachel's on-and-off relationship with Ross's best friend, Chandler. Eventually, Chandler and Rachel get together and Ross and Rachel begin to date other people.
Rachel is often portrayed as a ditzy and flighty character, who is attracted to men based purely on their physical appearance. She is initially portrayed as quiet and shy, but as the series progresses her personality becomes more outgoing and she begins to stand up for herself. She is often the center of attention, and the other characters often make fun of her. Rachel is often the one who initiates conflicts and arguments between the group, and she is often seen as the instigator of the group's troubles.

## Background

Povenmire was born on May 12, 1956 in Hutchinson, Kansas. He was an actor, puppeteer, and writer. He was a graduate of the University of Kansas with a degree in theatre. He is a member of The Second City Alumni. He has worked with Jim Henson, the Muppets, Walt Disney Imagineering, and the Walt Disney Company. In 1994, Povenmire began his career as a writer and story editor for the Disney animated television series Timon and Pumbaa. In 1999, he and Jeff Marsh began working together as co-creators of the Disney animated television series Phil of the Future.

In the 1990s, Povenmire was a puppeteer on the children's television series The Muppets at Home. While working on Timon and Pumbaa, he met and worked with Jeff "Swampy" Marsh. In 1999, Povenmire and Marsh began developing an idea for a show about a teenage boy from the future who travels back in time to meet his parents. They pitched the idea to Disney in 2000 and it was picked up for production. The show, Phil of the Future, debuted in 2004, and ended its run in 2006.

In 2006, Povenmire and Marsh created a pilot for a new show called The Replacements, which was picked up by Disney. The Replacements was cancelled, but Disney decided to produce a pilot for a new show called Phineas and Ferb. The pilot was produced in 2006 and the show was picked up and premiered in 2007. Povenmire served as executive producer for the show from 2007 to 2011, and Marvel Animation Studios took over in 2011. Phineas and Ferb has won several awards, including the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Children's Program and the Annie Award for Best Animated Television Production.

In 2008, Povenmire began working as a consultant on the Disney Channel Original Series, The Suite Life on Deck, which features Povenmire's wife, Alyson Stoner, as a series regular. Povenmire's daughter, Morgan, has also appeared in the show. In 2011, Povenmire and Marsh created the animated series Kick Buttowski: Suburban Daredevil for Disney XD. In 2012, Povenmire and Marsh created the animated series Gravity Falls for Disney Channel.

Once Dylan was well enough to resume creative work , he began to edit D. A. Pennebaker 's film of his 1966 tour . A rough cut w

ound up showing Dylan singing "Spanish Harlem Incident" on the roof of the Statler Hotel in New York City. In the middle of the song, Dylan suddenly stops, saying, "Don't make me do that again. I just can't do it." The audience hears this as an announcement that he's finished singing, but it's actually a reference to the fact that Dylan's voice is cracking as he pushes it to the breaking point. (This was a common and well-intentioned practice in live performance for singers, even as recently as the 1980s and 1990s.) The film's final title, _Eat the Document_ , came from a song that Dylan had written and rejected for the _Blonde on Blonde_ album, and may have been intended as an ironic comment on the film's cancellation. _Eat the Document_ had been scheduled for wide release in 1967. But the film was withdrawn from circulation when Dylan's manager, Albert Grossman, and Dylan's wife, Sara, objected to the film's use of a Beatles song, "Tomorrow Never Knows," which had been released on the Beatles' _Revolver_ album. The song had been taken from a tape Grossman had made of a song session at Olympic Studios in London. Dylan was the first of many artists to complain about the unauthorized use of their music in films, and the incident resulted in a long-standing animosity between Dylan and Grossman.

In 1795 , François Alexandre Frédéric visited Spanish Hill while en route to Canada . He described the hill as " a mountain in

the middle of a plain 100 km from Quebec City , whose summit was covered with moss and lichen , and whose flanks were covered with trees , ferns , mosses , roots of trees , boulders , and rocks. The whole thing was a veritable botanical garden ."
 The mountain was then called Montagne de Chien (Dog Mountain). It was renamed Mont Royal in 1804 by the British authorities.
During the 19th century, the mountain was a place for rustic picnics and summer parties. In 1876, the first trail was built to facilitate the ascent of the mountain. The early 20th century saw the construction of the Automobile Club of Canada and the first cable car which was replaced in 1966 by the funicular and the Mont-Royal Metro station. The mountain was to be the site of an Olympic Games. During the interwar years, the project was cancelled.
The mountain has been a park since 1918. It was classified as a National Historic site in 2001.
The mountain has been a popular tourist attraction since the late 19th century. In 2015, it was visited by 2,592,000 visitors.

Mutinus elegans is saprobic — deriving nutrients by breaking down dead or dying organic matter . It is commonly found in garden

beds, among leaf litter and other organic matter including rotting fruit on the forest floor.
The fungus is a cosmopolitan species found throughout the world, although it is reportedly more abundant in temperate regions.
The species was first described scientifically by the German mycologist Elias Magnus Fries in 1833 as Agaricus elegants. The name was transferred to M. elegans in 1962.
The specific epithet elegans means "graceful, elegant" in Latin.
The fruit bodies are short-stemmed, reaching a height of 4 to 12 cm (1.6 to 4.7 in) and diameter of 2 to 6 cm (0.79 to 2.36 in). They are initially convex, later becoming flat and then finally becoming slightly depressed in the center. The cap is covered with fine, white, dry hairs. The young fruit bodies are usually white but may be yellowish or reddish in color. The cuticle is blackish to gray, but usually has white or creamish patches.
The spores are elliptic in shape, measuring 6 to 8.5 μm in length and 4 to 5.5 μm in width.
The fungus is saprobic and grows on decomposing organic material, typically wood and leaf litter. It has been found growing on oak leaves that were exposed to the sun, but mainly colonizes decaying wood in the forest understory. It is found in Australia, England, France, and Italy.
The fungus is considered to be edible, although it is uncommon.

The Black Prince was commissioned in 1904. She was a successful cruiser and took part in the Battle of Jutland in 1916. She was very fast for an armoured cruiser and could shoot very accurately. She was involved in a naval battle with the German armoured cruisers Blücher and Von der Tann. She fired at the Blücher and damaged her. The Black Prince was then hit by a shell from the Von der Tann and sank. Only 36 of her 850 crew survived. She is remembered for her heroic actions in the Battle of Jutland and for the loss of her crew.

The Nine Queries , as they came to be called , focused on the divine right ( jure divino ) of church government . While the pre

amble and the first article of the document did not explicitly mention the pope or the papacy , the other articles were clearly directed against the papacy. They were written in an angry style and were intended to be read in the church, where the faithful were supposed to gather for the purpose of reading the documents to each other.
We have to admit that this is a rather strange and even obscure way of writing, since it does not invite the reader to follow the arguments closely. But it was precisely this way of proceeding that made the 95 Theses so effective. They were completely in accord with the spirit of the time, which was more and more dominated by an appealing style of preaching.
That style began to transform preaching in the churches, which had previously consisted of very long, complex, and hardly understandable sermons. A new, appealing style of preaching emerged, and it was achieved by means of a kind of rhetorical trick, namely, a question.
If you ask a question, you immediately attract the attention of your audience. If you then begin to answer the question, you can be sure that your audience will not lose interest in your words. This is the reason why the 95 Theses were so successful, as they were intended to be read in the churches, where the faithful were supposed to gather for the purpose of reading the documents to each other.
The preamble of the 95 Theses begins with the words " On the day and in the year 1517 . . . " ( Super in die septimo et anno MCCCCCXCVI . . . ). This is a clear reference to the feast of All Saints, which is celebrated on November 1. The purpose of the preamble was to place the theses within the context of church history, as if to say, "This is what the church has always believed."
The preamble is followed by an explanation of how Martin Luther discovered the truth behind the 95 theses. He did so, the explanation says, by studying the Bible and by listening to the Holy Spirit. The preamble concludes with a plea to the faithful to join Martin Luther in his efforts to reform the church.
The first article of the 95 Theses, " Our Lord Jesus Christ, on the night before He suffered, when He had supper with the apostles, and as He had given them the cup of the new covenant, after He had taken the bread and given thanks, He gave it to them saying, take, eat, this is My body, which is given for you. Likewise also the cup after supper saying, this cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is shed for you and for many for the remission of sins . . . " ( Quia transacto tempore noctis, quum manducasset cum apostolis, et quum eis manducavit panem novum factum, postquam gratiarum actione manducavit, dedit eis dicens, accipite, quodcumque hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis traditur, et pro vobis factum est, haec autem caput novum instrumentum novi testamenti, quem pro vobis factum est propter remissionem peccatorum . . . ).
This is the first of the nine queries , as they came to be called, which are directed against the preaching of indulgences. The first query is based on the words of Christ at the Last Supper, as recorded in the Gospels of Matthew ( 26:26ff. ) and Mark ( 14:22ff. ).
The query emphasizes the central theological question: What does the body and blood of Christ mean?
This is a basic question of Christian theology. It has been debated since the days of the early church fathers, and the answer to it has always been the same. The body and blood of Christ are the means of grace in the Christian church. Communion is the means by which the church receives the grace of God.

In the summer of 1945 several hundred veterans of the battle were detached from operations in Norway and returned to Arnhem to

1.75 miles south-west of Oosterbeek, the town that had been the scene of the final struggle. In the months that followed various events were held to commemorate the sacrifices of the men who had died, and now, in July 1946, the Dutch Government decided to erect a monument at the site of the 1st Airborne Division's bridgehead. The 1st Airborne Division Memorial at Arnhem was opened on Tuesday, 15 July.
The monument, which is a simple stone cross, lies a few hundred yards downstream from where the paratroops landed on 17 September 1944. Its base is inscribed with the names of the divisions that served with the 1st Airborne Division at Arnhem.
The 1st Airborne Division Memorial was unveiled by Brigadier G. E. R. Spurling, O.B.E., M.C., representing the British Army. Brigadier R. E. Dempsey, M.C., representing the Airborne Forces, was also present.
The Nijmegen Bridge, the site of the battle, is now best known as one of the bridges over the Rhine crossed by the Allied armies on their way into Germany.
1.75 miles to the south-west of Oosterbeek is the Arnhem–Nijmegen road, and about 2 miles to the east of this road is a large, open area known as the Arnhem Military Cemetery. The Arnhem Military Cemetery, which is the final resting place of more than 1,700 men and airmen, is the largest Commonwealth cemetery in the Netherlands.
The 1st Airborne Division Memorial at Arnhem is situated at grid reference 51°59' 57°26' and is about 2 miles from the best point of view of the Arnhem Bridge over the Rhine.

1.1 THE ORIGIN OF THE BATTLE
In July 1944, with the Allied armies advancing rapidly in France, the British Prime Minister, Winston S. Churchill, began to think about ways of launching a surprise attack across the Rhine before the Germans had a chance to build strong defences on the opposite bank. He therefore ordered the Combined Chiefs of Staff to prepare a plan to seize a bridgehead across the Rhine.
The Combined Chiefs of Staff were in favour of a joint seaborne assault, but the seamen felt that this was too risky, and they suggested that the operation should be carried out by an airborne force. It was decided to carry out a trial landing for this airborne operation on Heligoland, an island in the North Sea. This trial landing was successfully carried out on 26 August, and the Combined Chiefs of Staff then agreed that the airborne force should be made up of two divisions.
The Germans were also concerned about the Allies crossing the Rhine, and they placed a lot of effort into the task of building up strong defences on the other side. However, they did not fully appreciate the extent of the Allied resources, and they allowed the construction of the defences to be carried out with insufficient urgency.
The Allies had to find a site for the temporary bridgehead that would be just far enough inside Germany to be safe from German counter-attack, and just far enough inside Holland to give the paratroops a good start in the attack. Arnhem, with its bridge across the Rhine, was an obvious candidate for this, and it was therefore decided to use Arnhem as the British part of the bridgehead.

'I think the Liberals will soon have a majority, but it will be a small one.' Rosebery's prediction proved accurate, and in May 1886 he had to face Gladstone at the dispatch box for the first time as leader of the Liberal party.
Rosebery's new position as Liberal prime minister and leader of the Commons was one he had always coveted. During the 1860s he had been embittered by Gladstone's preference for Disraeli as chancellor of the exchequer. Rosebery's objections to Disraeli were both personal and political, and he had never forgotten Gladstone's preference for Disraeli. As the years passed, and Gladstone became more and more a national hero, Rosebery looked less and less likely to become prime minister. In 1876, when Gladstone had been out of power for four years, Rosebery wrote to a friend, 'Gladstone is the only man I ever heard of who can outshine himself.' By 1886, Gladstone had outshone himself twice, and he was regarded as the greatest prime minister in modern history.
Rosebery knew that the part he had to play was that of a 'moderating influence'. As he told Gladstone, 'It is the only course which can bring you and me together.' In the autumn of 1886 there was a general election, and the Liberals were returned with just over 400 seats. Rosebery's 'moderating influence' was to be put to the test. The new Liberal government was not ideologically driven, and there were few policies on which Gladstone and Rosebery disagreed. The two prime ministers met to discuss the first business of the new government – Ireland. Both men had worked for Home Rule for Ireland, and both felt that some form of self-government had to be granted to Ireland. Gladstone favoured a joint parliament, in which the two Houses would have equal representation. Rosebery favoured a single House, but he was prepared to compromise and accept a joint parliament.
The Irish question dominated the first year of the new government. Rosebery's 'moderating influence' was not always effective, and every time the Liberals came close to agreement Gladstone would make some new demand. The Irish leader Charles Parnell, who had long been confined to the Tower of London, was released in 1886 and the situation in Ireland became more volatile. The Irish Home Rule League demanded a new Irish parliament with full control over Irish finance and amendments to the constitution. Gladstone's response was to ignore the League, and he tried to enlist the help of the Irish landowners. He hoped that they would find a way of reducing the burden of the land tax which the League was demanding.
The Irish situation was always complicated by the fact that some of the main players were Roman Catholics. Gladstone and Rosebery, although both British by birth, were raised as Catholics. Gladstone's father had been converted to Catholicism in 1845, and Rosebery's father had been educated by Jesuit priests. It was not unusual to find British politicians who were Roman Catholics, but it was unusual to see a British prime minister who was a Roman Catholic. In 1886, Gladstone was an Anglican, but he had been brought up as a Catholic, and he had never ceased to admire the Irish Catholic landowners. Rosebery, on the other hand, was brought up as a Roman Catholic, and he was very suspicious of the Irish landowners. In 1886, Gladstone and Rosebery both wanted to help the Irish landowners, but they had different attitudes towards them. Both believed that the Irish landowners were the best hope for peace in Ireland, but they had different expectations from them. He believed that the Irish landowners were self-seeking, and he thought that they were oblivious to the suffering of the Irish tenants. Rosebery was more interested in the government's relationship with the tenants, and he believed that the government should help the tenants to assert their rights and demand their land.

In 1833 the British Association for the Advancement of Science commissioned a series of magnetic measurements across the United

Kingdom. The Royal Society's _Report_ of the survey indicated that from the Isle of Man to the southern tip of Cornwall, the magnetic declination was about zero. In the Bristol Channel, however, it was about 10 degrees west of north.
This was so significant that, in 1836, the Royal Society set up a Magnetic Committee to investigate the cause of the local deviation. The committee found that the magnetic declination was not constant but varied from year to year and season to season. The variation was due to the Earth's magnetic field interacting with the Earth's electrically charged atmosphere, which in turn responded to the Sun's magnetic field.
The Bristol Channel was a particularly good place to observe the effect. A local magnetic storm in 1836 caused compasses to deviate by almost 3 degrees and caused the ships of the Royal Navy to lose their bearings. The storm was not a one-off phenomenon, however, as the committee discovered. There had been earlier storms in 1832 and 1834.
The committee did not know that these magnetic storms were caused by a solar event. They did, however, publish their findings in what became known as the _Bristol Channel Letter_ , which was presented to the British Association for the Advancement of Science on 12 September 1836.
The _Bristol Channel Letter_ was widely circulated. Many scientists and astronomers were familiar with the event and it became, perhaps, the most famous scientific report of its time. In particular it was read by the young Charles Darwin, who later recalled that
This paper was sent to me in the year 1836 by a friend in the Navy, as an interesting case, and I then wrote it out in full on a separate sheet. I sent it to a scientific journal, and it was soon afterwards published in the _Philosophical Magazine._ It was afterwards translated by me into German, and published in the _Wochenschrift für die Erfahrungswissenschaft._
A few weeks after the _Bristol Channel Letter_ had been published, the young Darwin was on a ship, the _Beagle_ , sailing around South America. He was a keen scientist, and he was fascinated by the magnetic variation in the Bristol Channel. In his autobiography, Darwin suggests that the mystery of the storms was solved by the young William Thomson (Lord Kelvin). Kelvin had been studying the magnetic variation on ships of the Royal Navy, and he was the first to note that the magnetic variation in the Bristol Channel was in phase with the Sun's magnetic field.
Darwin would not be the last man to be influenced by the _Bristol Channel Letter_ , however. It also made a significant impact on Samuel Morse, and it was the impetus for him to invent the telegraph.
The _Bristol Channel Letter_ was published in the _Philosophical Magazine_ in March 1837. It was a remarkable paper for three reasons:
1 It was the first scientific paper to be written by a non-scientist. It was written by the Reverend Robert Haweis, a minister of religion and a popular inspirational writer.
2 It was the first scientific paper to be based on the analysis of data from observers of the general public. It was based on 164 observations made by sailors and merchants.
3 The _Bristol Channel Letter_ was the first scientific paper to be published by a woman. It was written by Mary Somerville.

The largest find of Iguanodon remains to that date occurred on 28 February 1878 in a coal mine at Bernissart in Belgium , at a

40-foot (12-metre) level. A total of 13 skeletons were discovered at the site in six different rooms, although at least four were only represented by bones. The German palaeontologist Ferdinand von Hochstetter was able to examine the fossils. He reported that the animals were so well preserved that even the original skin had survived, and that the bones had been deposited in mud and clay to make casts of them. The skeletons were taken out of the mine and transferred to the Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences in Brussels. They were described by Fernand de Loriol and Louis Dollo in 1882 as Iguanodon bernissartensis.

As of 1999 , Baltimore experienced 300 murders a year , which was the fourth most in the nation . Unemployment was 9 % , twice

the national average.
In 1999 , the 12th Street Taxi Company was founded by the former city's mayor .
In 2009 , Baltimore had the fourth highest murder rate in the United States .
In 2012 , Baltimore had 98 murders , an increase of 7% from the previous year .
In 2014 , Baltimore had the highest number of murders of any city in the United States , with 353 murders .
[5] In 2017 , Baltimore had 343 murders , an increase of 5% from 2016 .
The population of Baltimore is 614,771 , according to the 2016 Census . The city is the 29th most populous city in the United States .
 Baltimore is located on the Chesapeake Bay at the head of the Patapsco River .
 The city is located about 40 miles north of Washington, D.C., and is also a major seaport of the Mid-Atlantic region .
 Baltimore has been home to many important American industries and institutions .
The city's early growth was due in large part to its seaport , which helped make the city a major U.S. center for immigration and trade with Europe .
[7] Baltimore is also home to the Johns Hopkins Hospital and Johns Hopkins University .
 The city's other major employers include the Social Security Administration, Struever Bros. , Eccles and Rouse , and the Baltimore Symphony Orchestra .
The city is divided into nine geographic districts, including neighborhoods such as Charles Village, Harbor East, Mount Vernon , Hampden, Federal Hill, and Fells Point .
The city's major annual attraction is the Preakness Stakes , held at the Pimlico Race Course every May since 1870 .
 In 2007 , Baltimore was ranked second in the nation in the movement of young professionals to the city .
 The city was established by the Constitution of Maryland and is noted for its unique geographical location and urban planning.
 Baltimore is the largest independent city in the United States .

In 1972 , four years after the Chicago Great Western was merged into the Chicago and North Western Railway ( C & NW ) , the CGW

's 2-8-0 Consolidation steam locomotive #3490 was retired. The engine was placed on display at the C & NW's steam locomotive roundhouse in North Chicago , Illinois . Since the C & NW ceased operations in 1980 , the roundhouse and the engine have been turned over to the city of North Chicago . In 1985, the city decided to restore the locomotive to operating condition and run it on the city's railroad.
The engine was rebuilt and returned to service in 1990 , and was used to pull excursion trains on the city's railroad. The engine is the only one of its type in the United States that is operating.
The locomotive is on display at the North Chicago Main Street Depot. A plaque at the depot describes the restoration as well as the history of the engine.

An estimated 500 @,@ 000 burn injuries receive medical treatment yearly in the United States . They resulted in about 3 @,@ 300

hospitalizations and 3 @,@ 40 deaths. The majority of burn injuries result from accidents that occur in the home [2, 3]. The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission estimates that about 700,000 residential fires are caused each year by smoking and that 2,700 of these fires result in 600 deaths and 1,300 injuries .
It is impossible to prevent all residential fires, but there are many ways to reduce the risk of death and injury. A key component in the efforts to reduce residential fires is the installation of smoke alarms. Smoke alarms are the only effective means to warn occupants of a fire and provide enough time to escape .
In the United States , as many as one-third of the population lives in homes not equipped with smoke alarms . The National Fire Protection Association reports that 60 percent of home fire deaths occur in homes without smoke alarms .
The U.S. Fire Administration estimates that nearly 70 percent of all fire deaths and 80 percent of fire injuries are caused by home fires not reported by the family to the fire department .
The effectiveness of smoke alarms in reducing residential fire deaths and injuries has been proven time and time again. The National Fire Protection Association estimates that smoke alarms cut the risk of death by half in a fire in the home . The U.S. Fire Administration estimates that working smoke alarms cut the risk of death by half in fires in homes with smoke alarms and cut the risk of injury by half in fires in homes with smoke alarms .
Because smoke alarms have proven to be such an effective means of reducing fire deaths and injuries, the U.S. Fire Administration recommends that they be installed in every home .

SMS Markgraf was the third battleship of the four @-@ ship König class . She served in the Imperial German Navy during World Wa

r I. SMS Markgraf was named after the German title for a duke and was the third of four ships of the German battleship König-class (Kaiser Friedrich III), which comprised the most powerful warships of the German Imperial Navy. The ship was laid down on 28 March 1909, launched on 26 August 1910 and commissioned on 1 October 1911.
SMS Markgraf was assigned to the I Battle Squadron of the High Seas Fleet in 1913, and was part of the fleet that attempted to break the blockade of the British Grand Fleet in the Battle of Jutland on 31 May 1916. The ship was damaged by shellfire and spent the rest of the war in port. After the war, the ship was interned at Scapa Flow and was scrapped in 1920.
SMS Markgraf had two funnels, a light grey hull, and a waterline length of 160.1 metres (525 ft 4 in). The ship measured 223.0 metres (731 ft 8 in) between perpendiculars and had a beam of 27.8 metres (91 ft 3 in) and a draught of 9.1 metres (30 ft). She displaced 20,100 tonnes (20,000 long tons) at load and 20,700 tonnes (20,400 long tons) at deep load. At full speed, SMS Markgraf could make 21.5 knots (39.8 km/h; 24.7 mph). She had a cruising range of 6,000 nautical miles (11,000 km; 6,900 mi) at a speed of 10 knots (19 km/h; 12 mph), and SMS Markgraf was able to steam for 1,100 nautical miles (2,000 km; 1,300 mi) at 20 knots (37 km/h; 23 mph). The ship was fitted with three 3-cylinder vertical triple expansion steam engines that drove three propeller shafts. They were powered by 24 coal-fired marine range boilers and had a rated power of 26,000 metric horsepower (26,000 bhp; 19,000 kW) that powered the ship to a top speed of 21.5 knots (39.8 km/h; 24.7 mph).
SMS Markgraf was the third of four ship-class ships of the German battleship König-class, the most powerful warships of the German Imperial Navy. The ship was laid down on 28 March 1909, launched on 26 August 1910 and commissioned on 1 October 1911. She was named after the German translation of the English title Duke. SMS Markgraf's sister ships were König, Kronprinz and Kurfürst.
The ship was armed with ten 28 cm (11 in) Krupp guns in five twin turrets, each mounted on the centreline. The turrets were grouped 2–2, with the forward and aft turrets superfiring over the turrets on the centreline. Over the next few days, Jose continued to strengthen, reaching its peak intensity on September 5 with winds of 140 mph (220 km/h), the equivalent of a Category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Scale.  After that time, Jose gradually weakened, and was downgraded to a tropical storm on September 8.  On September 10, the system degenerated into a tropical wave.

Hurricane Jose

The storm also caused $200 million in damage.  In the Dominican Republic, the storm killed 10 people.  In Puerto Rico, the storm caused $1.9 million in damage.

In January and February 1984 , conditions were favorable for tropical cyclogenesis in the southwest Indian Ocean , including wa

- ters off the west coast of Australia. In a two-month period, 10 tropical cyclones were generated within a 1,500 km (900 nm) radius of 0°E. In addition, two tropical cyclones moved into the region from the southeast Indian Ocean . The ensuing severe rainfall and flooding caused major damage, costing an estimated .5 billion Australian dollars (1.1 billion U.S. dollars).
During the period of February 11-19, 1984 , La Niña conditions developed in the tropical Pacific Ocean , resulting in an anomalously warm sea surface temperature (SST) anomaly in the western Pacific Ocean . Subsequently, the SST anomaly in the western Pacific expanded in February and March, with the result that the number of tropical cyclone formations in the western Pacific increased and the number of tropical cyclones in the southwest Indian Ocean decreased. A review of the SST anomalies , coupled with the analysis of the geographic distribution of tropical cyclones, suggests that an anomalously warm SST anomaly in the western Pacific intensified the southwest Indian Ocean cyclone activity in February and March 1984 .

anbeyan–Braidwood Road .
The fort was built in 1837, during the period of the First Burmese War (1824–1826), and managed to survive the Second Burmese War (1852). It was the first British fort built in Australia.
The fort was the first military stronghold built in Australia by the British Empire . It was built in 1837 in response to the fear of a Burmese invasion of New South Wales . The fort was built at the same time as the nearby Eumeralla Stockade because of the tensions between the indigenous Nguraiillum and the European settlers in the area.
The fort was built by convict labour, under the leadership of the District Surveyor, John Russell. The fort was designed to be the strongest possible because of its strategic position. It was built to repel an expected attack from Myanmar .
The fort was designed to have three gates, each guarded by a man-trap. The fort was well defended with a moat and a high wall. The fort's main purpose was to control the roads that led to the south-east.
The fort becomes obsolete during the 1840s, when the threat of attack from Myanmar was diminished. However, it was maintained as a military base until the 1860s, when it was abandoned as a general army post.
The fort was restored in 1971 and is now a museum. It is operated by Queanbeyan City Council and has a small collection of artefacts. It does not have an entrance fee. The fort is open to the public every day of the year from 9:00am until 5:00pm.

Kremenets Castle is a historic castle in Kremenets, Ternopil Oblast, western Ukraine. It was built in the 14th century by King Casimir III of Poland on the Vovk River, 30 km south of Ternopil.
The castle was first mentioned in 1352. After the 1362 Union of Kremenets, it became the center of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. In 1372, Tarnov and Kremenets were united under the rule of the Polish king, Casimir III.
In 1404, the castle was captured by the Grand Duke of Lithuania, Vytautas, but was soon regained by Poland. In 1410, it was captured by the Teutonic Order. In 1411, it was captured by Lithuania, which held it until 1431, when it was regained by Poland. In 1434, it was captured by the Moldavian ruler, Alexander Dăneşteanu, who held it until 1441, when it was regained by Poland.
In 1442, the castle was captured by the Polish king, Władysław III, who held it until 1447, when it was captured by the Moldavian ruler, Petru Aron. In 1448, it was regained by Poland. In 1450, it was captured by the Moldavian ruler, Petru III Aron. In 1452, it was regained by Poland. In 1466, it was captured by the Moldavian ruler, Stephen III the Great, who held it until 1471, when it was regained by Poland.
In 1531, the castle was captured by the Crimean khan, Mehmed Giray. In 1535, it was regained by Poland. In 1556, it was captured by the Crimean khan, Devlet Giray. In 1576, it was regained by Poland.
In 1603, the castle was captured by the Chmielnicki Uprising. In 1609, it was regained by Poland. In 1648, it was captured by the Ukrainian Cossacks. In 1655, it was regained by Poland. In 1665, it was captured by the Ukrainian Cossacks. In 1667, it was regained by Poland.
Kremenets Castle was heavily damaged during the Crimean War.

The castle was built in the form of a square with four round towers at the corners and a 28-meter high eight-sided tower in the center. It had 12 towers in the walls. In the 17th century, the castle was rebuilt in Renaissance style.

In the 1980s , the political situation in Yugoslavia deteriorated , with national tension fanned by the 1986 Serbian SANU Memor

andum and the 1986–1989 Kosovo Crisis . By 1990, Serbs constituted 64.9% of the population of the Socialist Republic of Serbia , whereas in the Socialist Republic of Montenegro they constituted 44.9%. By contrast, in the Socialist Republic of Croatia, the most advanced republic in the Yugoslav federation, Croats constituted 82.4% of the population.
 In the 1980s , the Serbian leader Slobodan Milošević launched an anti-democratic campaign, in which he nationalised the Serbian media, and, in 1989, he began to refer to the Serbian language as the "language of the nationality", rather than the "language of all Serbs".
 In 1987–1988, Milošević launched a campaign to gain control over the Serbian Academy of Arts and Sciences . The campaign led to the removal of the academy's president, Dobrica Ćosić , and to the elevation of Milošević's chief ideologue Aleksandar Vasović to the presidency. Ćosić had been a prominent dissident theoretician of political pluralism in Yugoslavia. The campaign led to a breakup of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia into seven national and autonomous communist parties.
The Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts (SASA, Serbian: Srpska Akademija Nauka i Umjetnosti/Српска академија наука и уметности, SANU, Serbian Cyrillic: Српска академија наука и уметности) is a Serbian scientific and professional society founded in 1841. SASA has over 600 members, out of which, 225 are full members, 236 are corresponding members and 150 are foreign members. SASA includes 67 scientific institutions, and the number of its employees is more than 3500. This is the largest scientific organisation in Serbia with the largest number of members and scientific institutions in the country.

Joseph Michael " Joe " Nathan ( born November 22 , 1974 ) is an American professional baseball pitcher for the Chicago Cubs of

​​ Major League Baseball ( MLB) . He bats and throws right.
He played college baseball for the South Carolina Gamecocks baseball team of the University of South Carolina. He was chosen in the tenth round of the 1997 MLB draft by the Cubs.
In 1999, he made his MLB debut and played for the Cubs until 2010. He then played for the Tampa Bay Rays and the Cincinnati Reds. In 2013, he signed with the New York Yankees, but was released after only 20 games.
Nathan made his Major League debut on April 30, 1999, playing for the Chicago Cubs against the Pittsburgh Pirates . In 2001, he won a total of 15 games and lost 6 games.
In 2004 he helped the Cubs win their first National League (NL) pennant in 95 years and play in the World Series against the Boston Red Sox. He was the Cubs' closer and saved three games in the NLCS , but lost in Game 7 of the World Series .
In 2005, he saved 41 games, which made him the major league leader in saves at the time.
In 2006, he again saved 41 games. In the 2006 American League Division Series , Nathan saved two games against the Detroit Tigers.
Nathan signed with the Tampa Bay Rays on December 10, 2007 and retired in 2009. For the Rays, he saved 15 games and had a 2.89 ERA ( earned run average ).
After his retirement, Nathan worked as a broadcaster for the Rays.
Nathan played for the Cincinnati Reds in 2010.
On November 23, 2012, Nathan signed a one-year contract with the New York Yankees . He was released on May 20, 2013 after only 20 games. He had an ERA of 3.93 and an earned run average of 4.05.
In August 2013, Nathan filed a $ 4 million lawsuit against the Cubs organization. He accused the Cubs of unjustly terminating his contract. The Cubs claimed that Nathan had not met the requirements of his contract.
Nathan's brother-in-law, Jeff Suppan , is a former MLB player.

Terry Bazarian (born March 6, 1951) is a Canadian businessman and social activist. He is the co-founder of the Richmond First Association, which focuses on the development of poverty reduction strategies for the city of Richmond, British Columbia and the co-founder of the Institute for Social Innovation and Impact Investing at the University of British Columbia .
Born in Montreal, Quebec, Bazarian moved to Vancouver in 1975. He worked for twenty years in the private sector as a management consultant and entrepreneur with the accounting firm Deloitte, the Canadian stock exchange, and the United Nations International Development Organization .
Bazarian is a former Richmond City councillor. In 2002 he co-founded the Richmond First Association (RFA) with Rob Macdonald and other community leaders. The Richmond First Association is a social advocacy group that has done work on poverty reduction, affordable housing, and sustainability on the Lower Mainland. Bazarian served as the chair of the association from 2002 to 2010. A 2004 report by the association on Richmond’s poverty rates found that 14.2% of the city’s population lived in poverty. The report also found that the city had a 13% poverty rate, which is higher than other cities such as Vancouver with a 11.2% poverty rate.
In the 2005 civic election, he was again elected, though his Richmond First party only won three of the eight seats. He unsuccesfully ran for office again in the 2008 Vancouver municipal election on the Vision Vancouver ticket. In 2010, he was appointed director of the Institute for Social Innovation and Impact Investing at the University of British Columbia.

Over twenty skulls have been found from this dinosaur . As with other lambeosaurines , the animal bore a tall , elaborate bony

"crown" of nasal horns (like a modern-day rhinoceros ) on the top of its head .
Fossils of a lambeosaurine have been found at many sites of the Late Cretaceous, including Alberta , British Columbia , Montana , North Dakota , Saskatchewan , and Wyoming in the United States, and Alberta , and British Columbia in Canada.
The earliest discovered lambeosaurine is the genus Hypacrosaurus from the Late Cretaceous, which lived in Alberta and Saskatchewan. The species H. stebingeri is the most common, but the species H. altispinus is often considered to be a distinct genus, Lambeosaurus, rather than a member of the Hypacrosaurus genus.
The most common type of lambeosaurine in the Northern Hemisphere, was the genus Centrosaurus, which lived in Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Montana . Many other lambeosaurine species have been discovered in the Northern Hemisphere, including the genus Chasmosaurus and the species Chasmosaurus belli , which lived in Alberta and Saskatchewan; the genus Tarbosaurus , which lived in Mongolia ; and the genus Monoclonius , which lived in Montana and Wyoming .
The only lambeosaurine known from the Southern Hemisphere is the genus Janenschia , which lived in South Africa . It was about the size of a small horse, with a skull that was about 1 metre (3 ft 3 in) long.
The nomenclature of the lambeosaurines remains in a state of flux, as more remains are being found and more species are being described.
The authors of the revised version of the book The Dinosauria in 2010 proposed keeping Lambeosaurus as a valid genus but elevating the species H. altispinus to a separate genus, Chasmosaurus, as it was very distinct from the other lambeosaurines. Another scientist, reclassified the species Chasmosaurus belli as a new species of Lambeosaurus, Lambeosaurus lambei.
 In the United States, the fossils of lambeosaurines are protected by the Paleontological Resources Preservation Act and the Archaeological Resources Protection Act.

Latin America 's history and culture , Alonso suggests , began with the loss of Bolívar 's dream of a united continent and as a

result of the triumph of the most " rapacious " among its rulers. Rapacious , in Alonso's view , is a term that describes the behavior of a group of local oligarchies that are, in turn, dominated by the United States . In the words of Alonso , " the United States is the only great power in the world capable of financing the wars , the coups , the dictatorships , and the parties that keep the rest of the world poor and weak ." This vision of foreign and local oligarchs in cahoots is a theme that Alonso repeats throughout the book , but it is never more explicit than in the final chapter , " The United States: Parasite or Host?"
While Alonso has always been a supporter of the Cuban Revolution , he is no apologist for the Castro regime . He is highly critical of its methods of political control and its failure to develop a genuinely revolutionary culture . The book is generally critical of the Revolution 's economic and social policies . Alonso is especially concerned about the regime's long-standing failure to understand the role of culture in national development , and he is equally critical of the Cuban people 's failure to engage in a constructive internal debate about Cuba 's national identity and its relationship to the world.
In the final analysis , the book is a call for the people of Cuba to rebuild their society and their economy on the basis of a more pluralistic and inclusive vision of national development . The revolution, Alonso suggests , must begin with the Cuban people and not with the state . The state and the revolution are but two sides of the same coin . The Revolution cannot become a dictatorship and a functioning democracy .
This is a thoughtful and thought-provoking book that challenges the reader to think about the relationship between culture and development and the role of the state in promoting national development . Alonso argues that the Revolution must transform its economic and political institutions and that the people of Cuba must create a culture of inclusion and solidarity . Alonso 's argument challenges the Castro regime to rethink its approach to national development . It also challenges the people of Cuba to rethink their relationship to the state and to the Revolution .
